definitions.explanation: A hall or space for practicing martial arts, traditional arts, or spiritual disciplines. Also used figuratively for any place of serious training or learning.

examples.japanese: {道場|どうじょう}で{稽古|けいこ}する。
{父|ちち}は{剣道|けんどう}の{道場|どうじょう}を{開|ひら}いている。
examples.english: My father runs a kendo dojo.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}から{近所|きんじょ}の{柔道|じゅうどう}{道場|どうじょう}に{通|かよ}い、{礼儀|れいぎ}と{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{学|まな}んだ。
examples.english: Since childhood, I attended the local judo dojo and learned manners and technique.

notes:
Literally "place of the way" ({道|みち} + {場|じょう}). Originally a Buddhist term for a place of practice, it became associated with martial arts training halls.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道場|どうじょう}に{通|かよ}う (attend a dojo)
- {道場|どうじょう}を{開|ひら}く (open a dojo)
- {道場|どうじょう}{破|やぶ}り (challenging a dojo — showing up to fight its members)
- {道場|どうじょう}{主|ぬし} (dojo master/owner)

The word has been borrowed into English as "dojo." It is used for {剣道|けんどう}, {柔道|じゅうどう}, {空手|からて}, {合気道|あいきどう}, and other martial arts. Figuratively, places of rigorous training in cooking, comedy, or other fields may be called {道場|どうじょう}. Not to be confused with the homophone {同情|どうじょう} (sympathy).
